title: Pelvic support & surgical planes anatomy
description: The surgical map: ureter under uterine artery, uterosacral and cardinal supports, broad ligament folds, ovarian pedicle and pelvic floor.

questions.question: What is the difference between the broad ligament and pelvic support ligaments?
questions.answer: The broad ligament is a peritoneal fold. Cardinal and uterosacral connective tissues, together with pelvic-floor muscles, contribute substantially to uterine support.

questions.question: Why is the ureter important in pelvic surgery anatomy?
questions.answer: The ureter travels near the uterine artery and cervix. Understanding their relationship helps explain why surgical planes require careful identification.

questions.question: What is the broad ligament?
questions.answer: Double peritoneal sheet draped over uterus, tubes and associated structures. Function: Supports relationships but is not the main mechanical uterine support.

questions.question: Where is the mesosalpinx located?
questions.answer: Broad ligament portion related to uterine tube. Function: Supports tube and its vessels.

questions.question: What is the function of the round ligament?
questions.answer: Function: Helps maintain anteversion; not principal apical support. Band from uterine cornu through inguinal canal to labium majus.
